name: Duke Pre-College Programs
description: A variety of Duke-hosted summer programs that help students strengthen academic skills through interactive learning, teamwork, and exposure to new fields of study.

name: NCSSM Summer Accelerator
description: An intensive summer learning experience offering challenging STEM-focused courses taught by experts, where students collaborate with peers and engage in real-world applications.

name: NCSSM Summer Ventures
description: A fully funded summer program for academically strong North Carolina students that emphasizes hands-on research, university-level learning, and exploration of STEM career paths.

name: NCSSM INSPIRE
description: A research-focused summer program that introduces students from diverse backgrounds to STEM fields while building leadership skills and experience solving complex, real-world challenges.

name: EXPLORE@UNC
description: A one-week residential program that allows high school students to experience college life, sample academic subjects, and reflect on potential majors and career interests.

name: NC State Engineering Residential Camps
description: A residential summer experience where students live on campus at NC State while exploring a specific engineering discipline through hands-on projects and college-style learning.

name: NC State Engineering Day Camps
description: Week-long, non-residential engineering camps that introduce younger high school students to how engineers approach problem-solving across multiple disciplines.

name: UNC Chapel Hill Dual Enrollment
description: Eligible honor roll high school juniors may apply to take UNC summer courses as visiting students through the university’s Summer School program.

name: NC State College of Engineering Summer Research Experience
description: The Electrical and Computing Engineering Department at North Carolina State University is hosting a Young Scholars program for high school students from June 22 to July 20, 2026. Students will work with teachers and researchers to create and test lessons connected to current engineering research, including applied artificial intelligence.

name: Project SEED
description: This program supports high school students from diverse backgrounds by offering hands-on STEM learning and chemistry research opportunities. It provides summer research placements and virtual camps that focus on college readiness, lab skills, and exposure to chemistry careers.

name: Leadership Institute for Future Teachers (LIFT)
description: The Leadership Institute for Future Teachers (LIFT) is a six-day invitational program for rising North Carolina high school seniors interested in education, offering hands-on school experiences and exposure to education careers.

name: UNC School of the Arts Summer Intensives
description: The University of North Carolina School of the Arts offers immersive summer programs for middle and high school students across disciplines such as animation, dance, drama, film, music, and visual arts. Programs include hands-on training, performances, and instruction from professional artists, with additional online academic options and community camps available.

name: North Carolina Governor’s School
description: A prestigious, tuition-free residential summer program recognizing academic excellence in humanities, social sciences, and STEM.

name: Durham YouthWorks
description: Durham YouthWorks is a hybrid program that helps young adults build essential skills and explore career opportunities with local employers while earning stipends for participation.

name: Carolina Sports Journalism Camp
description: The Carolina Sports Journalism Camp at UNC-Chapel Hill is a program for rising high school juniors and seniors interested in sports and media, offering hands-on training in sports writing, broadcasting, photography, and newsroom practice.

name: Chuck Stone Program
description: The 2026 Chuck Stone Program is a four-day, in-person journalism workshop for rising high school seniors, offering hands-on reporting, newsroom practice, and mentorship while producing a collaborative multimedia publication.

name: NC State Design Camp
description: Design Camp is a pre-college summer program by NC State’s Design Lab that introduces middle and high school students to design thinking and its real-world impact through hands-on, creative experiences.

name: Horticultural Science Summer Institute
description: The Horticultural Science Summer Institute at NC State is a hands-on, residential program where high school students explore plant science, sustainable agriculture, and horticulture careers through workshops, field visits, and campus life experiences.

name: NC State Study Skills
description: The NC State Psychoeducational Clinic offers in-person and online programs that help students improve organization, study skills, and academic habits.

name: NC State Teen Writers Workshop
description: The Teen Writers Workshop is a two-week summer program that supports creative writing development and connects students with a community of young writers.

name: NC GlaxoSmithKline Foundation Program in Biotech
description: The North Carolina GlaxoSmithKline Scholars Program supports biology majors at UNC Asheville who demonstrate academic excellence and financial need, with a focus on undergraduate research in fields such as cell biology, biochemistry, and molecular biology.

name: Durham Public Schools Scholars-At-Work Program
description: The DPS Scholars-At-Work Program offers Durham Public Schools students in grades 10–12 a short-term workplace immersion experience, providing hands-on exposure to local companies and career paths.

name: Durham Aquatic School Lifeguard Instructor
description: DAS provides free lifeguard certification training for individuals ages 16 and older, preparing participants for aquatics careers and recruitment for lifeguard positions at DPR indoor and outdoor pools.

name: Durham Aquatic School Water Safety Instructor
description: This course certifies participants ages 15 and older to teach American Red Cross water safety and Learn-to-Swim programs. Certification requires passing a swim skills pre-test and completing the Red Cross online coursework.

name: Launching Emerging Employees Progarm (LEEP)
description: The LEEP program supports youth through paid entry-level jobs and career development, combining hands-on work with weekly soft-skills training across multiple Durham County Government departments.

name: MaryAnn Black Summer Internship
description: The MaryAnn Black Summer Internship Program offers students hands-on exposure to over 70 healthcare careers through hospital visits, interactive sessions, and skill-building workshops. Hosted by Duke Health with Durham YouthWorks, the program includes mentorship from Duke professionals and introduces career pathways across medicine and nursing.

name: Duke University Neuroscience Experience (DUNE)
description: DUNE provides local high school students with full-time, paid summer research opportunities in neuroscience labs at Duke University, offering hands-on experience, professional development, and mentorship, with no prior research experience required.

name: NC State College of Natural Resources High School Summer Research Program
description: This program at NC State introduces high school students to forestry and natural resources through mentorship, career exploration, and research exposure, including seminars and participation in NC State’s Research and Creativity Symposium.

name: Duke's STAR Program
description: The STAR Program is a six-week, full-time summer experience at Duke that immerses students in academic and clinical research. Participants work with faculty mentors to conduct research, develop a paper, attend research-focused lectures and workshops, and present their findings, with optional physician shadowing for eligible students.

name: UNC’s Nutrition Research Virtual Internship Program
description: This four-week virtual program engages students from rising 9th grade through rising college freshman in lectures, mentoring, and scientific skill-building with NRI researchers. Participants create and present scientific posters on a chosen nutrition topic, gaining experience in communicating research findings.

name: North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University’s Research Apprenticeship Program
description: This two-week residential summer program at North Carolina A&T immerses rising juniors and seniors in food, agricultural, and environmental sciences through hands-on research with faculty mentors. Students live on campus, explore Greensboro’s cultural landmarks, receive a stipend upon completion, and pay only a small application fee.

name: Youth Conservation Crews
description: Youth Conservation Crews offer teens ages 15–18 paid summer opportunities to work on hands-on conservation projects across the state. Crews run for 3–6 weeks during June–August, with small teams led by trained crew leaders.

name: Duke Research in Engineering Program (DukeREP)
description: DukeREP is a seven-week, in-person research program that places students in Duke Biomedical Engineering labs for hands-on research with faculty and graduate mentors. The program includes seminars, workshops, and networking opportunities, with a focus on expanding STEM access for students from underrepresented and economically disadvantaged backgrounds.

name: Durham Sports Commission Internship Program
description: The Durham Sports Commission offers internship opportunities for students interested in gaining hands-on experience in the sports industry through business tactics.

name: NC State VetCAMP
description: VetCAMP is a five-day summer program at North Carolina State University run by the Veterinary Professions Advising Center that introduces students to careers in veterinary medicine. Since 2011, the camp has offered hands-on experiences such as animal clinics, livestock work, suture and dissection labs, tours of the College of Veterinary Medicine, and exploration of related NC State majors.

name: Teens Art Council North Carolina Museum of Art
description: The NCMA Teen Arts Council is a group of teen ambassadors who meet weekly from September through June. Members help plan teen takeovers and art exhibitions, participate in artist workshops, attend museum events, and explore careers in the arts.

name: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences: Junior Interpreters Program
description: As a Junior Interpreter, you serve as a museum ambassador by engaging visitors with hands-on science and real specimens on the museum floor. The program builds strong communication, public speaking, and customer service skills while providing practical experience in science education and outreach.

name: NC State Resource Conservation Workshop
description: The Resource Conservation Workshop is a weeklong, application-based program that immerses students in hands-on learning about natural resources and environmental management. Participants engage in field studies, tours, and career-focused activities, with opportunities to earn awards and scholarships.

name: Teen X-Treme Summer Camp
description: Teen X-Treme is a summer camp for ages 12–14 that offers a fun, interactive curriculum including arts and crafts, indoor and outdoor games, and character and leadership development activities. Participants attend daily and bring their own lunch and snacks.

name: Outset Medical Summer Camp
description: Outset is a one-week pre-college camp that gives high school students hands-on exposure to healthcare careers. Held on the UNC–Chapel Hill campus, students learn from physicians, medical faculty, and medical students while exploring fields such as family medicine, surgery, neurosurgery, pediatrics, dentistry, and pharmacy, combining medical training and simulations with social activities that build community among future healthcare leaders.

name: UNC-Chapel Hill: Summer School for Rising High School Seniors
description: This program allows rising high school seniors to enroll as Summer School Visitors at UNC–Chapel Hill and take rigorous college-level courses during the summer. Students must apply with transcripts, a personal statement explaining their course goals, and letters of recommendation. The accelerated courses require a strong commitment, with daily class sessions and several hours of additional work, and final grades appear on official UNC transcripts.

name: Project Uplift
description: Project Uplift offers high school seniors an immersive, full-day experience at UNC–Chapel Hill designed to connect students with the university community. Participants attend lectures and small seminars, interact with current students, faculty, and staff, and learn about the admissions and financial aid process while gaining a firsthand look at campus life.

name: Upward Bound
description: Upward Bound at UNC–Chapel Hill is a competitive program that supports about 100 high school students in building the academic skills and motivation needed to succeed in high school and pursue a bachelor’s degree. Participants receive academic enrichment, college preparation support, and mentoring, and must attend designated high schools while meeting federal income and educational background guidelines.

name: Emerson Waldorf School Summer Camps
description: Emerson Waldorf School Summer Camps offer outdoor-focused programs centered on arts, crafts, fort-building, sports, farming, and nature exploration. With intentionally small group sizes, the camps emphasize individualized attention while encouraging active days, creativity, and meaningful connections with nature.

name: Uplift PLUS
description: Uplift PLUS is a two-week residential program for North Carolina students who participate in Project Uplift, focused on academic enrichment and college preparation. Participants live on campus while taking an essay-writing course for college applications, engaging in leadership development and experiential learning, and connecting with current UNC students and university resources.

name: iHEAL Overnight Healthcare Leadership Camp
description: iHEAL (Interdisciplinary Health Education for Aspiring Leaders) is a free overnight camp for rising 9th graders that introduces students to healthcare careers in southeastern North Carolina. Through hands-on simulations, seminars, campus tours, and guest speaker sessions, participants explore health careers, social determinants of health, and leadership skills while building connections that continue through alumni mentorship and learning opportunities during high school.

name: NSLC Raleigh-Durham Summer Programs
description: The National Student Leadership Conference at Duke University offers immersive pre-college summer programs that help high school students explore potential careers and interests. Through hands-on simulations and experiential learning, participants gain real-world insight into different fields while experiencing life on a college campus.

name: NCMNS Teen Science Cafes
description: Teen Science Cafés bring teens together in an informal setting to explore science and technology through engaging presentations and interactive activities. Held monthly during the school year, each café features a scientist talk, hands-on activity, Q&A session, and time to connect with other teens interested in science. The program is recommended for ages 11–17 and is free to attend.

name: NCMNS Cafe Coordinators
description: Café Coordinators are student volunteers who plan and host the Museum’s Teen Science Cafés, monthly events that highlight cutting-edge scientific research and STEM careers. Coordinators work with guest scientists to organize the programs, select topics, manage outreach and marketing, and develop skills in science communication, leadership, and public speaking while helping make these teen-led events possible.

name: NCMNS Junior Curators
description: Junior Curators are volunteers with a strong interest in conservation, animal care, and field biology. Participants support the Museum’s conservation efforts by assisting with educational programs and events, participating in field experiences and service projects, and helping care for the Museum’s live animal collection.

name: NCMNS CLIMATE RESILIENCE CAMP
description: Climate Resilience Camp is a week-long STEM enrichment program for students entering grades 9–12 that explores the impacts of natural disasters and extreme weather. Through hands-on activities on topics like extreme heat, flooding, and air quality, students investigate ways to strengthen community resilience, connect with professionals in climate-related fields, and are encouraged to lead a service project in their community during the school year.

name: Liberation Out Loud
description: Liberation Out Loud is a program for high school students that encourages them to use their passions and talents to support their communities and promote social justice. Participants connect their interests with opportunities for community service, collaboration, and advocacy while working toward collective liberation.

name: Wake County 4-H Teen Council
description: Wake County 4-H Teen Council helps teens develop leadership, communication, citizenship, financial management, and resilience skills. Members meet monthly in a youth-led environment to plan educational programs, organize community service projects, and participate in social activities while working with diverse peers.

name: Raleigh Summer Youth Employment Program
description: The Raleigh Summer Youth Employment Program (RSYEP) gives teens ages 15 to 18 the opportunity to gain hands-on experience and prepare for their future through paid work with the City of Raleigh. Over the course of eight weeks, participants explore different career paths while building valuable professional and life skills for success in today’s workforce.

name: Biogen-MIT Biotech in Action: Virtual Programs
description: This virtual program uses online labs, digital learning tools, and live discussions with professionals from Biogen and MIT to explore biotechnology and innovation with a focus on Alzheimer’s disease.

name: Fayetteville State University SOAR Program
description: Fayetteville State University is proud to host the Thurgood Marshall College Fund’s SOAR Program, a prestigious opportunity for rising high school seniors who demonstrate strong leadership and academic excellence. This week long immersive experience introduces students to college life while helping them build academic and professional skills through hands on learning and preparation for future success.

name: NC Central Science and Research Summer Program (SRSP)
description: The Science and Research Summer Program (SRSP) gives high achieving high school students hands on research experience by working with North Carolina Central University science professors across a range of disciplines. Open to students the summer before their senior year, the program introduces participants to real research environments while encouraging interest in STEM careers and helping them explore NCCU as a potential college choice.

name: NC House Page Program
description: This program gives high school students the chance to learn about and take part in the state’s legislative process through a four day immersive experience. Students in grades 10 through 12 observe how laws are made and gain the unique opportunity to work in the House Chamber during live legislative sessions.

name: NC Senate Page Program
description: The Senate Page Program gives high school students the opportunity to learn about and take part in the state’s legislative process. Students in grades 10 through 12 gain firsthand insight into how laws are made through this immersive experience.

name: Computer Science High School Internship Program
description: During the summer, participants take part in a computing boot camp to strengthen their skills in advanced block based programming and generative AI, mentor middle school science teachers in integrating computing into their classrooms, and develop creative curricula like simulations, games, and narratives that connect computer science with other scientific topics.

name: NC State Shelton Challenge
description: This six day summer program at NC State University is designed for rising 9th through 12th graders with a minimum 3.0 GPA who are interested in developing leadership skills. The $700 cost includes meals, lodging, and curriculum, and camps are offered in June and July with registration required before the first of each month.

name: NC State Summer Textiles Exploration Program (STEP)
description: The Summer Textile Exploration Program (STEP) at the Wilson College of Textiles at NC State University offers four one week sessions for rising high school seniors interested in fashion, engineering, chemistry, design, marketing, and the textile industry.

name: Wake Electric Youth Tour
description: Open to juniors only, the Youth Tour in Washington, D.C. brings together 1,500 high school students from across the country to learn about electric cooperatives, American history, and the U.S. government. Participants visit historic sites and federal institutions, connect with their congressional delegations, and become eligible for a $1,000 scholarship upon enrolling in a North Carolina college, along with additional scholarship opportunities, with applications typically due in mid December.

name: WakeWorks Youth Apprenticeship
description: Youth apprenticeships are work based learning programs for high school students age 16 and older that provide hands on experience in real work environments. Participants also take free dual enrollment classes at Wake Tech that count toward both high school and college credit, with career pathways available in fields such as manufacturing, engineering, automotive, and skilled trades.

name: Young Writers Workshop at the University of North Carolina Wilmington
description: Held in July, this intensive four day program brings young writers together with graduate students and professionals to strengthen their writing, communication, and collaboration skills while encouraging creative expression. Modeled after college level workshops, participants share their work and receive constructive, supportive feedback from peers in fiction, nonfiction, and poetry.

name: Youth Legislative Assembly
description: YLA is a three day mock legislative program where high school students debate issues and vote on topics related to local, state, and national government. Modeled after the North Carolina General Assembly, the session concludes with a final report that is shared with the governor and state legislators.

name: Free Enterprise Leadership Challenge
description: The Free Enterprise Leadership Challenge (FELC) is a low cost five day summer program for high school students entering grades 10 through 12, held on college campuses across the country, including two in North Carolina. Participants run their own business using real money and make decisions that determine whether their business succeeds or fails.

name: Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program
description: The Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program is an eight week summer internship for students interested in aquatic science that pairs participants with a local mentor in fisheries science. Sponsored by the American Fisheries Society, the program provides hands on experience through fieldwork and lab research, including activities such as fish population surveys, water quality testing, electrofishing, and habitat restoration.

name: AgDiscovery at North Carolina State University
description: AgDiscovery is a free two week program sponsored by the USDA that introduces students to careers in animal science, veterinary medicine, and agribusiness. Participants live on the NC State campus and take part in hands on labs, field trips, and workshops while learning research techniques from professors and professionals such as plant pathologists, entomologists, botanists, and veterinarians.

name: Meredith College High School Writing Workshop
description: This five day workshop gives high school students the opportunity to work with Meredith College faculty who are published writers while developing their creative writing skills. Participants explore genres such as fiction, personal essay, and poetry, collaborate with peers, receive one on one feedback, and present their work at an open mic and reception on the final day.

name: NC State Young Investigators' Summer Program in Nuclear Engineering
description: This residential program allows high school students to explore nuclear engineering through lectures, labs, and industry field trips. Participants work in small groups on topics such as nuclear waste management, radiation detection, and nuclear security while engaging with college level material and gaining insight into careers in the field. The program concludes with a final project presentation.

name: Conservation Corps North Carolina (CCNC) – Youth Conservation Crews
description: Youth Conservation Crews give teens ages 15 to 18 the opportunity to take part in conservation projects across the state during the summer. Running from June through August, these programs last three to six weeks and include small teams of four to six members led by two crew leaders.

name: IFAL (Institute for Future Agricultural Leaders)
description: The Institute for Future Agricultural Leaders (IFAL) is a one week summer program for rising high school seniors interested in agriculture, leadership, and career exploration. Participants connect with NC State faculty, explore different agricultural fields, take part in service projects and leadership sessions, and visit research farms and industry sites while building teamwork, communication skills, and a deeper understanding of careers in agriculture and environmental science.

name: The Hope Center at Pullen Internships
description: This internship program connects foster youth with personalized paid opportunities that help spark long term career interests and encourage high school completion. Participants can earn $10 per hour for up to 200 hours while working with businesses and nonprofits across the Triangle, with support provided for scheduling, transportation, and changes in foster placement to ensure access and success.
